links.outcome: Segmentation performance (DSC) on external prospective test cohort versus retrospective cross-validation
links.effect: Trained on retrospective cohort of 115 patients (30 scanners), tested on prospective cohort of 51 patients (7 scanners); test DSC 0.72 ± 0.16 vs cross-validation DSC 0.61 ± 0.03 for 2D-SegResNetVAE.
links.quote: The first cohort (cohort 1 - retrospective) was used for model training, and the second cohort (cohort 2 - prospective - ATEZOLACC clinical trial ( NCT03612791 )) was used for testing in both segmentation and classification tasks.

links.outcome: Segmentation performance variation across scanners/centers and opacified versus non-opacified images
links.effect: Opacified DSC 0.70 ± 0.17 vs non-opacified 0.74 ± 0.10; 3 of 4 worst-scored (class C) cases originated from the same center; 17 of 51 poorly delineated cases came from different machines/centers.
links.quote: However, 3 out of 4 cases scored as C originated from the same center, indicating a potential connection.

links.outcome: Ability of radiomics-based failure detector to flag poor AI contours, compared with clinician scoring
links.effect: LR detector on test cohort: precision 0.88, recall 0.75, accuracy 0.86; only 65.6% (21/32) of clinician grade A cases classified as no failure; 75% (3/4) of grade C cases detected.
links.quote: Specifically, 65.6% (21/32) of cases were correctly classified as A (no/minor correction), and 75.0% (3/4) as C (complete correction), including samples refused during segmentation scoring by the radiation oncologist.

links.outcome: Clinician review of AI segmentations of real patient images against predefined A/B/C criteria
links.effect: Oncologist scored 62% (32/51) A, 27% (14/51) B, 5% (3/51) C; 2 declined for low quality; mean correction time 4.26 min vs about 16 min manual.
links.quote: Additionally, based on qualitative results, specifically, 62% (32/51), 27% (14/51), and 5% (3/51) of the images in the test set (cohort 2) were scored as A, B, and C, respectively.
